findings.reason: The protected Python solution evaluates move costs for both valid target layouts: [0, 1, ..., n-1] (zero at start) and [1, 2, ..., n-1, 0] (zero at end). For each layout, it decomposes the permutation mapping into disjoint cycles: cycles of length L containing the zero element cost L - 1 moves, while cycles of length L > 1 without zero cost L + 1 moves. The solution runs in O(n) time and O(n) space; no candidate is required.

A permutation mapping index i -> target_pos(nums[i]) decomposes into disjoint cycles. The zero element acts as the single swap slot: a cycle containing zero rotates in L - 1 moves, while an external cycle requires 1 move to enter zero into the cycle and 1 move to exit, costing L + 1 moves total. Taking min over both target layouts strictly minimizes moves.
Tracing cycles for each target layout visits each position once, taking O(n) time total and O(n) auxiliary space for the seen array. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts nums permutation array, handles n=2 edge cases, and returns minimum moves to reach either sorted layout.

The approach accurately details cycle decomposition, empty-space cycle cost (L - 1), external cycle cost (L + 1), dual target layout evaluation, and O(n) time / O(n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover legal swap simulations, quadratic unindexed searches, single-target fallacies, already-sorted arrays, fixed points, external cycles, and n=2 bounds.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical permutation cycle decomposition algorithm for both zero-at-start and zero-at-end layouts with SHA-256 digests c7924149acc9855953b9afbba4ce2f880ec50851916b784fb071866f28d2c1ba and f8ce3eedaac88a1c2d0e3bd6b9553f7646dcce79ed602c1aaf02d2c2d9044f14.
